name: Toptal
what: A screened freelance network placing designers and Power BI / BI developers into long engagements with mid-market and enterprise clients.
howToWin: Apply into the vertical you are strongest in, not as a generalist — screening is run by domain experts and includes a live screen plus a test project. The Power BI and design verticals are separate doors into the same network, so a portfolio showing design craft AND working dashboards is unusually strong here.
caution: The funnel is brutal — fewer than 3% of applicants are accepted, and the test project is a significant unpaid time investment.

name: Braintrust
feeNote: "Zero platform fees for talent" (pricing page, checked 2026-09-09).
what: A talent network of vetted professionals serving 1,000+ companies across 100+ countries, with no commission deducted from your rate.
howToWin: Because nothing is skimmed, quote your true senior day rate rather than discounting. Demand skews to corporate teams needing brand systems, reporting and dashboards rather than one-off graphics.
caution: Public pages describe the vetting only in general terms, so the real bar and time to first contract are hard to judge before applying.

name: A.Team
feeNote: "You set your rate, and we don't skim it." Payment "twice a month on a Net-15 cycle".
what: An invite-and-referral network that assembles small senior teams ("missions") for companies, listing product designers alongside engineers and data scientists.
howToWin: Get referred if you possibly can — the page states every builder was referred or vetted and "We accept fewer than two percent of applicants". Position yourself as the design half of a product or data team, because work is bought as teams.
caution: The platform has pivoted hard toward AI and engineering work, so pure brand, editorial or print design is a poor fit.

name: Contra
feeNote: "Keep 100% of what you earn freelancing on Contra." Optional "upgrade to Contra Pro for $29/month". Clients pay a "$19 contract fee".
what: A commission-free professional network for independent creators, covering brand, graphic, web, product and motion design.
howToWin: Treat the profile as a portfolio site, not a bid page — it is public and indexed. A tightly edited set of brand systems and data-heavy case studies plus the "Get verified as an expert" step does more than volume applying.
caution: Open signup means no vetting filter, so you compete on portfolio quality alone and inbound can be thin without outside promotion.

name: Upwork — Expert-Vetted tier
feeNote: "The fee ranges from 0% to 15% per contract" (Freelancer Service Fee help page, checked 2026-09-09).
what: A very large open marketplace whose Expert-Vetted badge marks "the top 1% of talent on Upwork" after "a thorough pre-screening process by experts in their field".
howToWin: The badge is normally awarded when a field-specific Talent Manager invites you, so build a strong record in ONE narrow category — Design & Creative or Data Science & Analytics — until a Talent Manager reaches out. Badge holders get higher visibility to enterprise clients and access to privately posted projects.
caution: The open marketplace underneath is heavily price-driven, and the Expert-Vetted application window is usually closed, leaving invitation as the only route.

name: Fiverr Pro
what: The vetted business tier of Fiverr, where "Our industry experts evaluate every Fiverr Pro freelancer before they are accepted".
howToWin: You cannot self-apply — "you'll need to receive an invitation from our talent sourcing team". The realistic path is a high-rated seller record with long-term corporate clients, which is what the sourcing team screens for.
caution: A premium tier sitting on a marketplace otherwise known for cheap one-off gigs. Verify the seller deduction before pricing.

name: Superside
what: An always-on creative subscription company serving enterprise clients, running a deliberately small freelance roster alongside full-time creatives across 67 countries.
howToWin: Apply to a specific freelance listing. Expect three stages — talent partner conversation, take-home assessment with a skills presentation, then roster addition. Openings increasingly emphasise production systems and generative AI on top of Adobe and Figma craft.
caution: "We keep our roster small and selective", so freelance openings appear irregularly.

name: Reedsy
what: A curated marketplace connecting authors and publishers with book professionals — roughly 995 designers alongside editors, ghostwriters and translators.
howToWin: Submit a portfolio built specifically of interiors and covers — typesetting, grids, print-ready files. "Only the best freelancers make it into our community", and the design category is small enough that generalist branding work reads as off-target.
caution: Budgets are set by self-publishing authors and small presses, so per-project fees sit well below corporate identity work.

name: 99designs by Vista
feeNote: Platform fee by level: Top 5%, Mid 10%, Entry 15%; plus a "USD$100 introduction fee" on new client relationships.
what: A design marketplace running both speculative contests and paid 1-to-1 projects, with a Curation Team that assigns designer levels at signup.
howToWin: Ignore the contests. Use it only for 1-to-1 projects where you "Set your own prices" and payment is secured upfront. Climbing to Top Level cuts the fee to 5%, so early effort should go into level progression.
caution: The contest model is speculative unpaid work by design — poor value for a senior designer.

name: Malt
feeNote: "Malt freelance service fees are 5% (excl. tax)." Certain projects in France, Spain and Belgium may be 10% dropping to 5% after 6 months.
what: A European freelance management system with 850,000+ freelancers, used by large corporates to source, contract and pay independent designers and data specialists.
howToWin: Rates are quoted as day rates to corporate buyers, so publish a realistic senior day rate and aim the profile at in-house brand and BI teams. The 5% fee is low enough to price at market without padding.
caution: Europe-centred with a Paris head office and no stated Middle East presence, so demand and contracting assume an EU base.

name: YunoJuno
feeNote: "YunoJuno offers freelancers a fee-free experience"; "Full pay without the charges".
what: A freelancer marketplace and contractor-management platform used by global brands, spanning 15+ disciplines including Design, UX, Creatives, Studio, Film & Motion and Data.
howToWin: Since the platform takes nothing, set your rate at true market level and complete the profile against a named discipline. Bookings come from in-house creative teams booking known day rates, so a clear rate card and stated availability matter more than long proposals.
caution: Demand is concentrated on UK and US clients, with offices only in London and New York.

name: freelancermap
feeNote: "0% commission fees"; membership tiers exist but tier pricing is not stated on the homepage.
what: A European project marketplace for IT and tech contract work where BI and Power BI contracts are posted as day-rate projects.
howToWin: Use this as a BI channel rather than a design one. Lead with Power BI, data modelling and reporting as headline skills and respond fast to DACH-region postings — the design category is very small (~308 projects) next to development (7,192).
caution: Heavily oriented to Germany, Austria and Switzerland; many postings assume German language or European contracting.

name: Data Visualization Society Jobs Board
what: A public jobs board "managed by the Data Visualization Society as public service to the field", searchable by keyword, location and employment type including contract and freelance.
howToWin: The highest-signal channel for information-design work. Filter to contract and freelance and lead with evidence you can both design and build — pairing Power BI delivery with editorial-quality chart design is rare there.
caution: Volume is low compared with general design boards, and many listings expect D3.js, Tableau, Python or R.

name: We Work Remotely
what: A large remote-only job board whose design section runs from Junior Designer through Senior Visual Designer, Staff Brand Designer and Head of Design.
howToWin: Filter for listings marked "Anywhere in the World" — the majority — and apply the same day, because these attract very high volume.
caution: Some roles are restricted to specific countries such as Canada or the US, so the worldwide-remote framing does not apply to every listing.

name: Dribbble Jobs
what: The job board attached to the Dribbble community, carrying remote, full-time and freelance roles in brand, motion, email design, illustration and creative direction.
howToWin: Hiring here follows the portfolio, not the application — clients browse shots and then invite. Post finished brand systems and editorial spreads consistently and keep the profile marked available for work.
caution: The community rewards visually polished single shots, which under-represents strategic, editorial and dashboard work.

name: Behance JobList
feeNote: "Get Behance Pro to Unlock" with "Access to exclusive opportunities"; Pro pricing is not stated on the JobList page.
what: Adobe's freelance opportunity board, listing project work across graphic design, web/UI, motion graphics, 3D/CGI, illustration and product design.
howToWin: Corporate and agency clients search by visual style, so publish full case studies with process rather than final images only, and respond while listings are fresh — postings run on 7 to 14 day windows.
caution: Some opportunities are gated behind paid Behance Pro, and briefs skew digital and illustration over corporate or print work.

name: SlideGenius
what: A presentation-design agency building investor, sales-enablement and executive decks for corporate clients, which recruits designers directly.
howToWin: Apply directly with a portfolio that is purely high-end presentation work — PowerPoint craft, master templates, data slides — since the listing asks for "a portfolio demonstrating high-end presentation design expertise". The page states they are "open to considering remote candidates".
caution: Agency contract work rather than a marketplace, so rates are set by the agency and no pay information is published.

name: Turing
what: A remote talent platform engaging people as independent contractors across software, data science and engineering, plus "domain experts" working on AI advancement.
howToWin: Apply into the data or domain-expert track rather than design, complete the skill assessments and live interviews, and present analytics and BI evidence — AI-training and evaluation work now pays domain experts well.
caution: Engineering and data heavy with little pure design demand, and it states "Turing doesn't provide VISAs".

name: Mercor
what: An AI-economy marketplace paying domain experts to evaluate, benchmark and train frontier AI models, advertising an "Average contracted rate $112/hr".
howToWin: Apply as an analyst or evaluator rather than a designer — listings run from "$50 - $70 / hour" up to "$120 / hour" — and lean on documented business-intelligence and reporting experience, which maps directly onto model-evaluation work.
caution: No design or data-visualisation roles were listed at the time of checking, so this is an income channel for the analytics half of your skill set only.

name: Coroflot
what: A long-running design job board and portfolio host covering graphic, product, industrial and UX design from intern to executive level.
howToWin: Use the seniority filter to skip everything below Senior, and pair each application with a hosted Coroflot portfolio since employers search that database directly.
caution: Listing volume is modest and heavily weighted to US locations.

name: Design Jobs Board
what: A design-only job board carrying graphic design, branding, art direction, creative direction and wayfinding roles at studios and agencies.
howToWin: Watch it for the occasional fully remote or freelance studio brief and for UK studio market intelligence. Applications land better when the portfolio matches the studio's sector.
caution: Almost all listings are London or UK-based and require hybrid or in-office attendance, which rules most of them out from the UAE.
